owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: Evicting buckets
requirements: idle buckets older than two minutes are dropped
the map is capped (10,000 keys) with oldest-first eviction
createServer exposes the limiter it builds as server.rateLimiter (read only, for tests), and exports MAX_BUCKETS = 10000; the limiter at http.mjs:108 is built with the cap
the cap bounds every key family the limiter holds (ip: and t: keys alike, and any map it splits into), checked after every take(), not only after a sweep

at the cap, eviction removes a bucket holding at least one token (least recently used first) before any exhausted bucket (fewer than one token); eviction is amortized O(1), never a scan of the map per insert, and a new key is always admitted

a bucket is idle when no take() touched it for 120,000 ms (time since its last take, b.at), and only idle buckets are dropped by the idle rule; any sweep timer is unref'd and cleared when the server closes

the remote rate-limit key follows the tunnel that actually carries the request, which the daemon passes into createServer (an activeTunnel() option set from the running provider, beside tunnelKey): through Cloudflare, quick or named, it is cf-connecting-ip, which Cloudflare's edge sets and overwrites; through a provider or relay whose client header is not verified, and with no tunnel, it is the socket address; remote.trusted_proxy, whose only accepted value is the string 'x-forwarded-for', means the last X-Forwarded-For element is the client address, and it applies only when no tunnel is active; an active tunnel always wins over it; IPv6 addresses are keyed by their /64. Tests that simulate distinct remote callers by header pass activeTunnel to createServer and change no assertion (memev twin finding F-2, red-team round 2 answers 1 and 10)

one rule decides which bucket a remote request takes: a request whose token verifies is limited by its token bucket (t:) alone; every other request (no token, a bearer or a /c/ path whose token does not verify, the OAuth and invite routes) takes the address bucket; an unverified token adds no t: entry, so a bearer header can neither skip the pre-auth throttle nor fill the limiter, and a token holder behind a flooded or shared address is never locked out

every structure the limiter keeps for ordering or eviction is bounded by the same cap as the map, and at the cap with every bucket exhausted a new key is still admitted by evicting the least recently used bucket
the test never asserts the value of MAX_BUCKETS and takes its loop bounds from literals, so the mutation check fails only when the cap stops being enforced
docs/CLOUD.md states the limit, which address each tunnel is limited by, remote.trusted_proxy and the per-token rule

the daemon passes the running provider into createServer: src/server/main.mjs builds the server with activeTunnel reading the provider the tunnel supervisor actually started (supervise exposes it), never a value a test supplies, and the request path spawns no process to find it
the limiter's counting API is size (every entry of every structure it keeps) and has(key); the cap and idle tests use only createServer, size and has

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/rate-limit.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest
